LESSON: Before wiring any new I/O into an existing hot-path call site, trace what that route's own header comment promises about cost/compute -- a 'just a SELECT, zero live compute' route is exactly where an unconditional new query, even one designed to fail gracefully, is the wrong default. Check slate/allowlist membership synchronously first; only touch the network when a genuine candidate exists.

A repo's own 'boot-proof' tests that regex-match literal import strings in a route file are a real, working control (they caught this card's wiring change immediately and correctly) -- but fixing one to pass requires understanding what GUARANTEE it was protecting (never bake/CAD/GIS/texas-rrc, transitively) and preserving that guarantee at the new location, not just updating the string it happens to match today.

'Structurally read-only' is not one fixed guarantee -- 'the code never issues a write' (a review-time convention) and 'the connection refuses a write at the Postgres protocol level' (default_transaction_read_only=on) are both real but meaningfully different strengths, and two modules in the same codebase can use the same phrase for either one. Worth checking precisely, not assuming, when a sibling module's header comment claims the same property.
